content:
Jada Williams: for the `explain` endpoint — Console needs a couple extra fields for the tooltips in cost breakdown UI. Right now we only get `breakdown` + `assumptions` but no short “why did this change” hints.

Jada Williams: examples of tooltips we’re trying to populate:
- “Compute cost higher due to low batch efficiency”
- “Cache savings limited; KV hit rate assumed (telemetry missing)”
- “Quant profile q4_k_m: expected -18% decode compute”

Dylan Brooks: +1. we can build copy from raw numbers, but the UI mocks expect a small list of “contributing factors” per component. ideally deterministic + same wording across tenants.

Chloe Martin: are you asking for *more* fields under breakdown components or a top-level list? we need to be careful about payload bloat; explain responses can get huge if we dump telemetry.

Jordan Lee: we intentionally kept v1 explain minimal (no “reason codes”) because of payload size + stability. but we can add something like `explanations` with codes/short strings.

Amara Diallo: heads up: gateway has response size guardrails. internal routes are more permissive but we still see perf regressions when responses exceed ~128KB. we should avoid returning large arrays of factors.

Jada Williams: understood. we don’t need raw telemetry series. just enough for tooltips. could be as small as:
- `component`: compute.prefill / compute.decode / memory / cache_savings
- `reason_code`: LOW_BATCH_EFFICIENCY / KV_HIT_RATE_ASSUMED / QUANT_PROFILE_DELTA_APPLIED
- `short_text`: one-liner
- optional `value`: like `batch_efficiency=0.62`

Logan Wright: please don’t put raw values that look like “customer identifiers” in there (route names, model ids are fine; tenant ids not). also, if you include any “top routes” type contributor list, cap to N=3 and aggregate rest.

Felix Schneider: from audit/compliance side: “why is cost high” *can* become sensitive if it reveals traffic patterns. tooltips should be generic, not “you sent 97% of traffic to route X”.

Dylan Brooks: for UI we only need generic reasons + maybe a couple numeric scalars (batch_efficiency, kv_cache_hit_rate, prefill_ratio) but those already appear in “advanced details” drawer. the tooltip just needs the English sentence.

Chloe Martin: suggestion: add a compact `tooltip_hints` field that’s designed for UI only.
Something like:
- `tooltip_hints`: list of strings OR list of `code:…; text:…` but not nested.
But we can’t do nested objects in some clients? (typescript types are fine, but some teams asked for “string-only details”).

Jordan Lee: nested objects are fine in JSON but our internal “error.details string-only” constraint doesn’t apply here. still, we should keep schema stable and avoid huge structs.

Ethan Park: let’s keep it structured (codes) so Console can translate/format and we don’t lock copy in the API. API can provide `reason_codes` + `metrics_used` (names only) + `assumptions_applied` (already present).

Jada Williams: if we only get codes, product/design asked for consistent user-facing copy. they don’t want Console inventing 12 variants and drifting from Optimize.

Dylan Brooks: ^ exactly. if the service owns canonical language, it’s also easier for Support to reference.

Ethan Park: ok compromise: service returns codes + a single short message per code (canonical English). Console can display the canonical message, but if we ever need localization/changes, we bump SCM minor.

Amara Diallo: payload size: can we make it opt-in? e.g. `GET /explain?include=tooltips` or request body `explain_verbosity: summary|full`.
Default stays lean.

Jordan Lee: +1 opt-in. we can also add a `max_hints` integer with server-side cap.

Nadia Rahman: please be explicit when a hint is driven by assumption vs telemetry. we’ve had confusion where people thought “kv hit rate low” was measured but it was defaulted.

Jada Williams: +1. UI wants to show “estimated” vs “measured” tag for a couple of these.

Chloe Martin: proposal for v1.1 (still under `x-redwood-scm-version: v1.1`):
- request: add `include: ["tooltips"]` (or `include=tooltips`)
- response additions:
  - `tooltip_hints`: array (max 10) of compact objects: `{component, code, message, source}` where `source in {"telemetry","assumption","model_catalog"}`
  - no free-form contributor arrays (no per-route lists)
  - if size would exceed limit, drop hints + set `tooltip_hints_truncated=true`

Amara Diallo: truncation flag is good. if we do object array, please keep field names short-ish. we’re already seeing some `explain` payloads near 60–80KB with large breakdowns.

Jordan Lee: breakdown size is the bigger culprit. some clients are sending 30+ components when they pass through their internal “dimensions”. explain is echoing too much. we should consider server-side collapsing.

Logan Wright: +1. we should not reflect arbitrary client dimensions back. that’s a cardinality footgun.

Dylan Brooks: for Console, we only ask explain for a single request summary (not high-cardinality). Optimize might do batch scenario sweeps though.

Jordan Lee: Optimize uses `estimate` mostly, not `explain`. still, adding tooltips to explain shouldn’t make “what-if” heavier.

Ethan Park: decision:
1) add `include=tooltips` support on explain (opt-in)
2) cap hints + add truncation boolean
3) hints must not include route-level or tenant-level contributor lists
4) every hint includes `source` so Console can label assumptions

Jada Williams: works for Console. I’ll sync with Design (DES-221) so they know what they’re getting.

Chloe Martin: can you share the exact UI sections mapping? want to ensure `component` naming matches.

Dylan Brooks: mapping we’re using:
- “Compute” section: prefill + decode
- “Memory/overhead” section
- “Cache savings” section
- “Other adjustments” (quant, retries)
We’ll send you the list of component keys we display.

Jordan Lee: I’ll open a PR to add the schema fields behind v1.1 + include flag. ETA tomorrow.

Amara Diallo: please also add a quick unit test that payload stays under size threshold with tooltips enabled. even just a synthetic worst-case.

Logan Wright: and pls ensure we’re not copying any raw telemetry blobs into `explain`. only derived scalars.

Nadia Rahman: +1 and document which scalars can show up (batch_efficiency, kv_hit_rate, prefill_ms/decode_ms) if we ever decide to include them later.

Felix Schneider: ping me when PR is up; I’ll sanity check that none of the new fields violate “customer-sensitive” guidance.

Jordan Lee: will do. I’ll tag Ethan + Felix on the PR.

Chloe Martin: thanks. also, let’s keep the copy short. anything longer than ~120 chars doesn’t fit tooltips well.

Jada Williams: cool. closing loop on my side once PR is up + we validate in staging.
